research_question: Distinguish transaction activity, gross payment value, collateral, custody, tokenized notional and net new capital across XRPL and its connected ecosystem.

claims: Bitquery counted approximately 7.82 million RLUSD account-to-account payments on XRPL in the 30-day window.
Approximately 7.79 million payments, reported as 99.6%, went from a 110-wallet cluster to three collector wallets, at an average payment of approximately 0.00099 RLUSD.

The cluster was funded with RLUSD from one Binance-labeled wallet and XRP from six Binance-labeled wallets; Bitquery describes the pattern as repeated withdrawal, dust-payment and return-deposit activity.
The 110-wallet cluster's 495 XRP fee cost was estimated at approximately $648 for 8.6 million transactions over the month.
The cluster accounted for 45.6% of all XRPL account-to-account payment count in the week of October 8-14 and then largely stopped between October 14 and 16.

issuer_loop.source_interpretation: Issuer mint/redemption plumbing accounts for approximately one-fifth of gross payment value.

classification_limits: The term 'bots' is Bitquery's behavioral characterization. The 110-wallet cluster is defined by common collector wallets and shared funding; no beneficial owner or operator identity is established.
Bitquery says every sampled dust payment carried the genuine RLUSD issuer token, but its stated sample covers one sender for one day, not every dust payment.

The article reports 14,600 payments of at least 1 RLUSD, then says 14,578 were genuine issuer RLUSD and 30 were look-alike tokens. Those counts sum to 14,608, an eight-payment internal discrepancy that remains unresolved.

The issuer loop table reports $734M from redemption wallet to issuer, while the following paragraph reports $744M paid to issuer. Preserve both reported values; do not silently reconcile the $10M difference.
The timing of the cluster shutdown and the October 15 Cross River announcement is temporal correlation only. Bitquery explicitly does not establish causation.
key_findings.interpretation: Payment count was materially inflated by a small-value, highly repetitive cluster. The remaining gross RLUSD value is large but concentrated in a small number of wallets and includes issuer mint/redemption and exchange/custodian-style deposit flows. It is not equivalent to $7.33B of net new capital, XRP purchases or independent end-user payment demand.

claims: Cross River announced a partnership with Ripple to integrate RLUSD into its Core Operating System, with support for transactions on XRPL.
The integration is intended to let eligible fintech businesses access USD/RLUSD conversion, cross-border payments and treasury movement through one API, alongside ACH, wires and real-time payments.
Cross River described RLUSD as an additional payment rail inside its regulated banking infrastructure.
key_findings.relationship_boundary: This is a direct Cross River-Ripple/RLUSD-XRPL integration. It does not establish that XRP is used as a bridge asset for every RLUSD payment or that payment volume creates net new XRP spot demand.

key_findings.methodology: Dashboard says balances are read daily from XRPL rippled account_info at approximately 08:00 UTC; exchange labels use XRPSCAN. Region means exchange headquarters, not customer residence.
limits: Most balances are pooled customer deposits in omnibus wallets, including cold storage.
Some exchange-controlled reserves, including cbXRP and Binance-Peg XRP backing, are included.
Unlabeled exchange wallets may be missing.
These balances are not order-book depth, corporate treasury holdings or immediately tradable float.
key_findings.interpretation: Upbit is the largest tracked exchange custodian by labeled XRP wallet balance; Coinbase is the largest tracked U.S.-headquartered venue. SBI VC Trade's 60M XRP is a pooled labeled-wallet observation, not proof of SBI treasury accumulation or new customer purchases.

key_findings.methodology: Same-wallet comparison removes wallets newly added to the tracked set; exchanges with incomplete wallet-set checks are excluded.
key_findings.limitation: A same-wallet balance decline can be customer withdrawal, exchange internal movement to a wallet not yet tracked, or wallet relabeling. It is not automatically a sale or a transfer to self-custody.

key_findings.methodology: TrackWhale says exchange flows count transfers between tracked exchanges and wallets outside the tracked exchange set; internal and exchange-to-exchange transfers are excluded. Only tracked large transfers are included.
key_findings.comparison_note: Direction is consistent with XRP Radar's negative same-wallet balance change, but the figures are not directly comparable and are not a full-market netflow series.

key_findings.interpretation: The 68.89B ledger-based proxy subtracts escrow and burned fees but does not necessarily subtract Ripple-held non-escrow operational XRP. It is not the same definition as CoinMarketCap's approximately 63.35B circulating supply. The estimated 70% re-escrow/30% use split is a historical tracker pattern, not a guarantee of future behavior.
This is holdings/AUM, not daily net inflow. Holdings dates vary by issuer and must not be treated as a synchronized point-in-time snapshot.

limits: Dashboard says totals use each protocol's oldest counted data date.
Wrapped representations are claims on underlying XRP, not additional native XRP supply.
Cross-category aggregation with exchange reserve balances may overlap; do not add all dashboard categories without checking custody/underlying relationships.

key_findings.interpretation: Only approximately $276M is described as transferable investor float. Approximately $4.06B is registry/represented notional for assets that cannot move wallet-to-wallet by design or regulation. The $4.33B headline must not be called freely tradable capital, deployed XRP liquidity or XRP demand.

key_findings.publisher: XRP Insights / XRP Radar citing t54 Labs
key_findings.interpretation: The dashboard says these are sub-cent micropayments. At a rough $1.24-$1.25 XRP reference, cumulative value is approximately $49K, not millions or billions. Transaction count measures service-call frequency, not capital deployed. The dashboard claims native XRPL Payments with source tag 804681468 and periodic rippled spot checks; this run did not replay the facilitator's complete transaction history.

key_findings.limitation: Company-reported figure attributed to SEC filings; not independently reconciled to a complete set of custody wallets or a fresh filing in this run.

claims: Circle's SEC filing says Circle and SBI Holdings each contributed approximately USD 1.5M equivalent in Japanese yen to Circle SBI Japan K.K. in November 2025.
The entity was established to support USDC distribution in Japan.
Circle owns 50% but consolidates the variable-interest entity because it directs the activities that most significantly affect the entity and bears potentially significant losses/benefits.
The filing says there had been no significant operating results to date as of June 30, 2026.
key_findings.interpretation: SBI Group has a direct 50/50-capitalized USDC distribution joint venture with Circle, but the filing's no-significant-results statement cautions against treating the JV itself as proof of material production volumes. SBI VC Trade's separate USDC distribution and JPYSC operations must be tracked independently.
key_findings.identity_boundary: Circle SBI Japan K.K. is not Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. (the separately identified Japanese SBIC company), and neither should be conflated with SBI Holdings.

key_findings.publisher: Nodal Clear / Ripple and Coinbase Derivatives
claims: Ripple and Nodal Clear announced Ripple Prime clients have access to the full suite of Coinbase Derivatives contracts cleared by Nodal Clear.
The announcement specifically includes institutional and nano-sized XRP contracts among the Coinbase Derivatives products.
Access is facilitated through Hidden Road Partners CIV US LLC, the FCM acquired by Ripple and renamed Ripple Prime.
Coinbase's current derivatives page lists Ripple Prime among broker distribution partners.
key_findings.interpretation: This is a confirmed institutional distribution/access relationship between Ripple Prime and Coinbase Derivatives, including XRP futures. It is stronger evidence than merely listing Ripple Prime as a broker partner.
unknowns: Actual Ripple Prime client positions, executed XRP futures volume and market share.
Whether client access caused incremental XRP spot demand or only hedging/derivatives exposure.

claims: Circle reported $655.3M in first-half 2026 distribution costs in connection with its agreements with Coinbase.
The corresponding second-quarter amount was $324.6M.

The filing says Coinbase allocations depend on USDC held on its platform after Circle's issuer retention and also include half of remaining broader ecosystem growth economics after approved third-party participant payments.
key_findings.interpretation: Coinbase is economically central to USDC distribution. The reported amount is Circle's expense under the agreements, not a direct measurement of Coinbase net profit. The formula also means Circle's economics are sensitive to USDC balances, reserve yields and approved ecosystem distributions.

claims: Permission identifies ASK as an omnichain LayerZero OFT token with official contracts on Base and Polygon.
Permission announced that its ASK wallet moved to Coinbase Embedded Wallet infrastructure.
Permission says Coinbase secures the private key, while the user's Permission login authorizes transactions; Permission says it no longer holds wallet keys.
Permission says email address, account identifier and wallet information are shared with Coinbase for wallet operation.
key_findings.interpretation: This resolves one strong ASK Coin candidate as Permission Coin (ASK) and establishes a direct Coinbase wallet-infrastructure relationship. No official ASK contract on XRPL was identified; this is not evidence of an XRP integration.

claims: Circle's Q2 2026 10-Q reports an average reserve return rate of approximately 3.49% in June 2026.

Circle's internal twelve-month sensitivity table estimates that a 100-basis-point increase from that yield would increase reserve income by approximately $737M and distribution/transaction costs by approximately $360M; a 100-basis-point decrease produces the corresponding negative changes.

Circle states that while reserve yield effects can be modeled, it cannot accurately predict how interest-rate changes affect reserve income because USDC circulation and end-user behavior are uncertain.
Circle says distribution costs payable to Coinbase and Binance are directly affected by USDC held on those platforms and by distributor actions and policies Circle does not control.
key_findings.interpretation: Circle's macro exposure is a joint function of reserve yield, USDC circulation and distribution mix. Lower rates can reduce reserve income, but the net effect on USDC circulation and Circle's economics is uncertain. The sensitivity table is a company model scenario, not a forecast or guaranteed outcome.

key_findings.publisher: Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.
claims: The official company profile gives the legal/trade name 東京中小企業投資育成株式会社 and English name Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. (SBIC East Japan).

The company was established November 15, 1963, has corporate number 9011001030621, and lists shareholders including 18 prefectural/local governments, chambers of commerce, financial institutions and operating companies.
Its June 12-13, 2025 two-day generative-AI and machine-learning training was restricted to investee companies; the official page says general companies could not enroll.
Day one included ChatGPT instruction. Day two included Copilot, RAG, APIs, prompt/business use and information-leakage risk.
key_findings.interpretation: This resolves the Japanese SBIC entity from its own corporate profile. The training is an investee-company education programme, not evidence of an OpenAI commercial partnership, a ChatGPT-SBIC product, an XRP project or an SBI Holdings relationship.
key_findings.identity_boundary: Tokyo SBIC is distinct from SBI Holdings, SBI VC Trade and Circle SBI Japan K.K.

claims: Coinbase reported USDC assets on platform of $8.874B at June 30, 2026, versus $7.485B at June 30, 2025, a 19% increase.
Coinbase reported first-half 2026 USDC rewards expense of $232.535M, including $119.108M in Q2.

Coinbase said first-half 2026 stablecoin revenue decreased by $113.4M due to lower average interest rates, partly offset by higher average USDC balances held by customers in eligible Coinbase products.

Coinbase reported total assets on platform of $245.866B at June 30, 2026; the 'Other' category was $36.478B and comprised various other crypto/payment-stablecoin balances, none individually above 5% of total AOP.
The 10-Q does not separately disclose XRP or RLUSD balances or XRP collateral utilization.
key_findings.interpretation: This provides primary SEC evidence that Coinbase's USDC platform balances grew while rate declines reduced stablecoin revenue. The Circle-reported $655.3M H1 distribution cost and Coinbase-reported $232.535M H1 USDC rewards expense are different companies' expense measures; they must not be subtracted to claim Coinbase net profit. The filing's broad 'Other' category does not permit an XRP-specific custody estimate.

claims: Nodal Clear expanded 24x7 clearing support for Coinbase Derivatives Exchange XRP futures on June 13, 2025.
The published 24x7 eligible product list identifies nano XRP futures (XRP) at 500 XRP per contract and XRP futures (XRL) at 10,000 XRP per contract.
Nodal Clear describes itself as the CFTC-regulated derivatives clearing organization for these contracts.
key_findings.interpretation: The Ripple Prime distribution relationship is built on an already operational 24x7 XRP futures clearing product set. Contract access is confirmed; actual Ripple Prime client positions and volume remain undisclosed.

claims: Coinbase reported 10.7% crypto trading-volume market share in Q3 2026 and its fourth consecutive quarter of share gains in spot and derivatives.
Coinbase reported 12.5% share of total crypto market capitalization by Assets on Platform.
Average USDC held in Coinbase products reached $22B, up 49% year over year; Coinbase said it captured approximately 50% of all USDC economics over the prior year.
Coinbase reported 179% compound annual growth in crypto derivatives trading volume over the preceding two years.
Subscription and services revenue represented 49% of Q3 net revenue; prediction markets exceeded $200M annualized revenue; average daily loan-book balance was up 74% year over year.
Coinbase said Base remained the leading L2 for spot trading and DeFi TVL as of Q3 2026.
key_findings.interpretation: Coinbase's competitive position is an integrated exchange, derivatives, custody, stablecoin-distribution, lending, onchain and prediction-market platform. These are company-reported performance measures, not independent market-share calculations. The release does not disclose XRP-specific custody, collateral balances, or Ripple Prime client XRP positions.

claims: Coinbase reported that 97%+ of onchain agentic transactions used its x402 protocol in Q2 2026.
Coinbase reported that 99%+ of onchain agentic commerce was completed using USDC.
Coinbase reported that 90%+ of agentic stablecoin transaction volume ran on Base.
Coinbase reported average USDC held in Coinbase products of $20B in Q2 2026 and approximately 50% of all USDC economics over the prior year.
key_findings.interpretation: Coinbase's x402/agentic payments strategy is USDC- and Base-centered according to its own Q2 release. XRP Ledger t54/x402 dashboard observations use a different facilitator, chain, payment population and measurement window; they are not directly comparable. This creates a competing payment-rail hypothesis, not proof that Coinbase's x402 displaced XRPL activity.

key_findings.publisher: Circle and Coinbase SEC filings / earnings releases
claims: Coinbase Q2 2026 Form 10-Q reports $8.874B USDC within its June 30 Assets on Platform table; Coinbase AOP excludes assets for which customers hold full or partial private keys.
Coinbase Q2 earnings release reports average USDC held in Coinbase products of $20B; Coinbase Q3 release reports $22B average USDC held in products.
Circle Q2 2026 Form 10-Q reports $12.442B USDC on Circle's own platform at June 30, 2026 and a 19.5% daily weighted-average share of total USDC circulation.
Circle defines its 'USDC on platform' as USDC in Circle Mint accounts, corporate-held USDC and non-custodial wallets offered through Circle. It is not a Coinbase-held balance.

Circle separately reports $655.3M H1 2026 distribution costs in connection with its Coinbase agreements; the agreement's allocation formula is based in part on USDC held on Coinbase, but the $12.442B Circle-platform figure is not that Coinbase balance.
key_findings.interpretation: These figures have different scopes: Coinbase point-in-time custodial AOP, Coinbase average product balances, and Circle's own platform balances. Circle's 19.5% share is Circle-platform share, not Coinbase share. The SEC filing separately discloses distribution costs paid in connection with Coinbase agreements but does not disclose a directly comparable Coinbase-held USDC balance in the cited table. Preserve each metric and definition; do not average or label Circle's $12.442B as Coinbase assets.

claims: Cross River said it integrated Ripple's RLUSD into its proprietary Core Operating System with support for XRPL transactions.
Cross River said eligible fintechs could move between USD and RLUSD, settle cross-border payments and treasury movements 24/7 through one API alongside ACH, wires and real-time payments.
Cross River said customers could access RLUSD through the API and that the service was available only in limited U.S. states at announcement.
The announcement described RLUSD market capitalization as above $2.5B and more than $1B issued on XRPL.
key_findings.interpretation: This is a direct Ripple/Cross River banking-infrastructure relationship and an announced RLUSD payment rail on XRPL. It does not establish XRP is used as a bridge for every RLUSD payment, nor does it disclose production payment volume or net new XRP demand.
key_findings.data_quality_note: XRP Radar's November 2 dashboard displays approximately $2.42B RLUSD supply. This is not directly reconciled with Cross River's October 15 'more than $2.5B' market-cap statement; dates, circulating-supply scope and methodology differ. Preserve both source claims rather than choosing one.

competing_hypotheses.claim: XRPL RLUSD payment counts substantially overstated broad economic usage during the 19 Sep-18 Oct window because a small dust-payment cluster dominated count.
competing_hypotheses.limitation: Bitquery's cluster attribution is behavioral inference; no beneficial owner or intent is identified.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Despite the dust cluster, the remaining RLUSD payment value reflects meaningful institutional settlement activity.
competing_hypotheses.supporting: Bitquery reports $7.33B across 14,600 payments >=1 RLUSD and 1,826 senders/1,536 receivers.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: 95% of gross value came from 828 >=$1M payments; top ten senders were 82%; issuer loop accounted for roughly one-fifth; some wallets look like exchange/custodian deposit accounts.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Cross River integration could expand RLUSD usage through regulated banking and fintech API channels.
competing_hypotheses.unknown: Actual production payment volumes, customer count, corridor mix, and the XRP-vs-RLUSD role in settlement.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Tracked exchange-wallet balances and large-transfer datasets suggest net XRP withdrawals from exchange-attributed wallets.
competing_hypotheses.supporting: XRP Radar same-wallet 7-day decline and TrackWhale large-transfer net outflow.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: Both methods have label coverage limitations; wallet rotation and untracked destinations can mimic withdrawals.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Institutional XRP adoption is broadening through ETFs, cbXRP, DeFi, custody and RWA rails.
competing_hypotheses.supporting: ETF holdings, cbXRP supply, DeFi locked XRP and XRPL RWA records.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: ETF holdings are not flows; cbXRP and wXRP are wrapped claims; RWA notional is mostly non-transferable registry value; DeFi/custody categories may overlap.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase's USDC/Base x402 ecosystem may compete with XRPL-based XRP/RLUSD agent micropayments for developer and merchant adoption.
supporting_evidence: Coinbase Q2 company release reports 97%+ of onchain agentic transactions using Coinbase x402, 99%+ of onchain agentic commerce using USDC and 90%+ of agentic stablecoin volume on Base.
XRP Radar/t54 dashboard reports 14.88M XRPL x402 transactions but only 7,022 XRP plus 40,389 RLUSD cumulative settled value.
counterevidence_or_limits: Different facilitators, chains, user populations, time windows and definitions; not directly comparable.
Coinbase's figures are company-reported aggregate metrics; XRP Radar's figures are a dashboard/operator aggregation not independently replayed here.
A chain-agnostic x402 protocol can support multiple settlement assets and networks; competition and complementarity can coexist.

Unique payer/merchant concentration and repeat payment rates.
Net external settlement after internal transfers and issuer mint/redemption.

source_independence_and_caveats: Bitquery's RLUSD analysis is one provider's onchain reconstruction; its source labels and cluster inference are not independent confirmations.
XRP Radar aggregates multiple primary sources but remains one dashboard; the raw source records and methodology must be independently replayed before predictive admission.
TrackWhale large-transfer flows and XRP Radar same-wallet balances use different inclusion rules and must not be numerically combined.
Cross River's press release is primary evidence of an announced integration, not proof of current production payment volume.
The 110-wallet cluster's shutdown around October 15 is timing correlation, not proof that Cross River's announcement caused it.

forecast.reason: These are market-structure and payment-quality findings. No point-in-time historical feature store, leakage-safe walk-forward evaluation, calibrated probability model or resolved shadow forecast series has been established.
